analysis.title: CTA Update
key_insights: CTA positioning changes over the past week were mostly in equities. Funds remain 'max short' US and European rates, 'max long' USD in all six FX pairs tracked, and 'max long' Oil vs 'max short' Gold.
The tech-led selloff took global indices through CTA sell signals. Funds were signaled to reduce SPX longs and flip short NDX, and are sellers of both SPX and NDX this week.
The next level for CTAs to flip short SPX is 7638, about 1% below the 7719 ESZ6 reference. A further selloff below 28455 in NQZ6 (-3.6% vs 29251) moves CTAs to 'max short' NDX.
CTAs remain 'max short' RTY, with the first cover level over 4% higher at 2848 (RTYZ6 ref 2738).
CTAs saw their final sell level in SX5E broken on the morning of the report. If levels hold they join the 'max short' positions in RTY and MXEF this week.
MXEF went 'max short' early last week. The cover level is over 3% higher at 1652 (MESZ6 ref 1600).
In Japan, CTAs were signaled to reduce NKY longs and flip short, and will be sellers this week. The final sell level for 'max short' NKY is 125.52 (JBZ6 ref 125.81).
CTAs remain 'max short' US Treasury futures despite last week's rally. Cover levels are 102-11 in TU (ref 101-28), 105-02 in FV (ref 103-29) and 106-25 in TY (ref 105-08).
European sovereigns are 'max short' with a buffer to the first cover level. The closest are Bunds at 122.08 (RXZ6 ref 121.37) and Gilts at 85.55 (GZ6 ref 83.90).
CTAs were signaled to begin covering JGB shorts, ending the global 'max short' duration position held since August. They flip long JGBs if the rally continues above 126.39 (JBZ6 ref 125.81).
CTAs hold 'max long' Oil as WTI futures return to April levels. A reversal of over 20% lower is needed before they reduce longs.
CTAs remain 'max short' Gold and Silver, with cover levels +4.5% and +10.6% higher respectively. In Copper they reduced longs last week and flip short below 652.76 (HGZ6 ref 657.9).

CTAs hold 'max long' USD in all six FX pairs, but sell-USD triggers have moved closer: USDJPY 63.57 (JYZ6 ref 63.49), GBPUSD 134.13 (BPZ6 ref 133.42), USDCAD 71.71 (CDZ6 ref 71.38). The EURUSD trigger is further away at 1.1505 (ECZ6 ref 1.1234).
risk_factors: A continued tech-led selloff would push CTAs to flip short SPX below 7638 and to 'max short' NDX below 28455, adding systematic selling.
A rally in USD pairs reversing toward the sell triggers (USDJPY 63.57, GBPUSD 134.13, USDCAD 71.71) would start USD long trimming by CTAs.
A further rally in US Treasuries toward the cover levels (TY 106-25) would trigger short covering by CTAs.
vol_and_positioning: CTAs are sellers of SPX and NDX this week after the tech-led selloff, moving to moderately long SPX and moderately short NDX.
CTAs are 'max short' RTY and MXEF, and SX5E joins them if current levels hold.
CTAs are 'max short' US and European rates, 'max long' USD across six FX pairs, 'max long' Oil and 'max short' Gold and Silver.
Citi's model has four regimes: 'max' short, moderately short, moderately long and 'max' long. A 'max' regime does not mean positioning has reached a historical max.
CTA positioning estimates are proprietary calculations and may not reflect actual CTA positioning or returns.
